diagnostics.message: :resource.google_monitoring_notification_channel.channels creates notification channels via the Cloud Monitoring API, which is not enabled by default; if monitoring.googleapis.com is being activated by :resource.google_project_service.project_services in the same apply, channel creation races the API activation and fails. Every other API-dependent resource in this module (quotas, compute metadata, sinks, service identities) declares depends_on on :resource.google_project_service.project_services, but this one does not.

:resource.google_monitoring_alert_policy.alerts is created through the Cloud Monitoring API, which must be activated via :resource.google_project_service.project_services before alert policies can be written. No attribute reference or depends_on establishes this ordering (the implicit dep on the notification channels only covers cases where channels exist), so on a first apply the alert policies can be created before monitoring.googleapis.com is enabled and fail.

:resource.google_monitoring_monitored_project.primary registers this project under a metrics scope using the Monitoring API (locations.global.metricsScopes.projects), which requires monitoring.googleapis.com to be enabled in this project. The API activation is performed by :resource.google_project_service.project_services, but this resource does not depend on it, so the two can race on a fresh project.

:resource.google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service attaches this project as a Shared VPC service project of an external host; the Compute API must be enabled in this (service) project before the association succeeds. :resource.google_project_service.project_services performs the API activation, and the sibling resources google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host and google_project_iam_member.shared_vpc_host_robots already depend on it, but this resource has no dependency on it and can be applied before the Compute API is active.

The explicit depends_on of :resource.google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.service_agent_cmek on :resource.google_project.project is redundant: its for_each keys and member values are built from local._cmek_members, which reads local._aliased_service_agents[dep].name/.iam_email, and that local chain resolves local.project.number from google_project.project[0]. Terraform already infers this dependency through the local-value references, so the explicit entry duplicates it.

The explicit depends_on of :resource.google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.service_agent_cmek on :data.google_project.project is redundant: the resource's members/keys derive from local._cmek_members via local._aliased_service_agents, whose email/number computation references data.google_project.project[0] (in the project-reuse branch of local.project). Terraform already tracks this as an implicit dependency through the locals, so the explicit depends_on entry adds nothing.
